comparison: Both strongly support PARP-1's direct binding to H4K20me1 in vitro (C2, C21, C22, C84). Peer reviewers explicitly call this one of three 'compelling experiments.' OpenEval emphasizes the high reproducibility (r=0.92) and convergence across multiple methods. OpenEval covers additional claims about ChIP-seq correlations (C27-C29, C31, C94-C96) that peer reviewers address separately in R3.

Both support the ChIP-seq evidence for PARP-1/H4K20me1 association (C27, C28, C29, C31, C94, C95). Peer reviewers describe this as 'convincing evidence' supported by biochemical and ChIP-seq analyses. OpenEval groups these claims with in vitro binding data, while peer reviewers evaluate the genomic correlation data as a distinct line of evidence.

Perfect agreement on combinatorial histone modification effects (C23-C26, C85). Both evaluations support the peptide array data showing bidirectional modulation and phosphorylation effects. Peer reviewers describe this as 'convincing' and 'compelling' without raising specific concerns. OpenEval provides more technical detail about the experimental evidence.

Both strongly support the PR-SET7 mutant phenotype and its similarity to PARP-1 mutants (C4, C32, C33). Peer reviewers explicitly identify this as one of three 'compelling experiments,' noting the phenocopy of developmental arrest. OpenEval additionally addresses molecular validation (C34-C36) that peer reviewers evaluate separately in R5.

Both support the molecular characterization of PR-SET7 mutants (C34, C35). Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge and note the contrast with human cell data is not problematic. OpenEval groups these with the developmental phenotype, while peer reviewers treat the molecular validation as distinct from the phenotypic observations.

Strong agreement on RNA-seq and ChIP-seq integration showing co-regulation (C37-C44). Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of 'convincing evidence' for the overall model. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of correlations and differential patterns, while peer reviewers accept the transcriptomic data without specific commentary.

Both support the gene ontology findings (C45, C46, C49), but OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval expresses concern that mechanistic proposals (C49, C91-C93) are speculative and lack direct causation evidence. Peer reviewers accept the functional interpretation without challenge, consistent with the developmental arrest phenotype.

Divergent evaluations of mechanistic models (C91-C93). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative and require additional functional validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, describing the manuscript as 'mostly complete' and accepting the models as reasonable interpretations that contribute to understanding.

Perfect agreement on human cell data showing evolutionary conservation (C47, C48). Both evaluations support the correlation between PARP-1 and H4K20me1 in human cells. Peer reviewers implicitly accept broader relevance beyond Drosophila, while OpenEval notes functional significance requires further investigation.

Strong agreement on heat shock gene expression defects in mutants (C51, C6, C69). Peer reviewers explicitly identify this as one of three 'compelling experiments,' noting the phenocopy of defective heat shock protein induction. Both evaluations accept the qRT-PCR data without challenge.

Both support the ChIP-seq data showing differential H4K20me1 patterns before heat shock (C52, C53, C54). OpenEval groups these with qRT-PCR data, while peer reviewers evaluate ChIP-seq and ChIP-qPCR data together. Both accept the dynamic changes as part of the heat shock response mechanism.

Both support the opposite H4K20me1 dynamics at different gene groups (C55, C56, C7). OpenEval notes the inference about regulatory significance is reasonable but questions whether H4K20me1 is truly dispensable for group B genes (C58). Peer reviewers accept the differential patterns without raising this concern.

Both address mechanistic interpretations of H4K20me1 dynamics (C57, C58). OpenEval expresses some skepticism about the dispensability claim (C58), suggesting the decrease could reflect active removal. Peer reviewers accept these interpretations as reasonable inferences without challenge.

Strong agreement on reduced PARP-1 chromatin association in PR-SET7 mutants (C59, C60, C8, C9). Peer reviewers explicitly identify this as one of three 'compelling experiments' showing dramatically reduced PARP-1 association. Both evaluations strongly support the immunofluorescence data as evidence for H4K20me1-dependent recruitment.

Strong agreement on reduced poly-ADP ribosylation in mutants (C63, C64). Peer reviewers explicitly endorse this as one of three 'compelling experiments.' Both evaluations accept the Western blot data showing dramatic reduction in pADPr without challenge.

Both strongly support the conclusion that PR-SET7/H4K20me1 is crucial for PARP-1 function (C61, C65). OpenEval emphasizes the dramatic difference in localization and pADPr accumulation. Peer reviewers describe this as part of the 'convincing evidence' for the central model.

Perfect agreement on the central conclusion (C10, C3). Both strongly support the model that PR-SET7/H4K20me1 recruits PARP-1 for transcriptional regulation. Peer reviewers describe this as identifying 'a new and important interaction' with 'convincing evidence.' OpenEval notes the conclusion is well-supported by convergence of multiple experimental systems.

Divergent evaluations of mechanistic hypotheses about H4K20me1 dynamics (C71-C73, C76). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative and lack direct experimental validation, particularly the proposed unidentified demethylase. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as reasonable inferences from the data.

Both address the functional redundancy hypothesis (C76). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting this requires further testing. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the model as a reasonable interpretation. This represents a key difference in how speculative mechanistic proposals are evaluated.

Divergent evaluations of the PARP-1 chromatin maintenance model (C79-C82). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model lacks direct experimental support and would require time-resolved studies. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, describing the manuscript as 'mostly complete' and accepting the model as contributing significantly to understanding.

OpenEval evaluates claims about prior work on PR-SET7 knockout mice (C74, C75) as SUPPORTED but notes an apparent contradiction with the authors' model that deserves more discussion. Peer reviewers do not separately address these literature-based claims.

OpenEval separately evaluates established background knowledge from the literature (C1, C11-C20, C30, C50, C62, C66-C68, C70, C77-C78, C83, C86, C89-C90) as appropriately cited context. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on novel findings.
